title: platform-standup-2026-03-18
body:
Date: 2026-03-18
Attendees: Alex Kim, Priya Sharma, Carlos Lopez, Maya Patel, Jordan Li, Samir Rao (ops)

Quick notes / agenda:
- Control plane migration status (schema + leader election)
- Routing policy rollout (region-aware fallback)
- Auth token expiry bug and quota enforcement anomalies
- Observability: dashboards + spike alert tuning
- Action items and blockers

Updates:
1) Control plane (Priya)
- Migration of config schema to v2 is ~85% complete. Remaining: two index-heavy tables (route_aliases, tenant_policies). We ran a dry-run on staging last night; found a query plan regression around alias lookups that caused ~3s p99 on a few requests.
- Mitigation: rewrite the alias upsert path (PF-4123) -> Carlos is on a quick fix PR. If merged today, schedule can still meet Friday cutover for non-prod.
- Leader election changeover: tested multi-zone leader failover; a corner-case raced when a partitioned db replica lagged >30s. Added extra safety to promotion logic; still need one more smoke test.

2) Routing (Carlos)
- Region-aware fallback policy v0.3 rolling to canary (10% traffic) in us-west1. Preliminary metrics look good: +8% API latency but +20% success rate for cold-started model instances due to better local fallbacks.
- Observed one mis-route where quota metadata mismatch caused requests to be routed to a cheaper variant incorrectly. Traced to stale cache TTL on route metadata (PF-4180). Fix is to invalidate on config-push; will include in next patch.

3) Auth & Quotas (Maya)
- Reported issue: several service-to-service tokens expired earlier than expected in the last rollout window. Root cause: token refresh job used TZ-localized time from a host with clock skew. Temporary fix: bumped refresh window + added monotonic clock checks. Long-term: add NTP verification in bootstrap (ops TODO).
- Quotas: noticed ~0.5% of requests bypassed per-route enforcement for a span of 2 hours yesterday. Likely cause: sharded quota cache lost a node during deploy; we had no automatic failover because the shard map update was delayed. Action: change rollout to include shard-map atomic swap and add health-check gating.

4) Observability / Ops (Jordan + Samir)
- Dashboards: added new per-tenant token-cost heatmap and per-route p99 latency panels.
- Alerts: reduced sensitivity on short-lived token-exhaustion alert to prevent noisy pages; still investigating root cause for quota-overdraft spikes.
- Capacity: Dedicated pools saw a spike during the canary; autoscaler handled it but we should tweak target headroom to avoid any 429 spikes under similar traffic patterns.

Decisions / Notes:
- Keep routing canary at 10% for 48 more hours. If no regression, move to 50% by Friday.
- Postpone control-plane production cutover until the alias upsert fix is merged and validated in staging.
- Ops to prioritize NTP/clock-sanity work next sprint (blocked until smaller infra patch lands).

Action items (owner + due):
- Carlos: merge alias-upsert hotfix PR and run staging smoke tests (due: 2026-03-18 EOD) [PR #678, PF-4123].
- Priya: coordinate final control-plane dry-run and schedule production cutover contingency (due: 2026-03-19).
- Maya: implement shard-map atomic swap for quota cache rollouts and add unit tests (due: 2026-03-24) [PF-4180].
- Jordan: tune autoscaler headroom for dedicated pools and create runbook for 429 spike mitigation (due: 2026-03-20).
- Samir (ops): add NTP verification to bootstrap images and roll to staging (blocked by infra-patch-#122).

Blockers:
- Infra-patch-#122 (node bootstrap change) is needed before NTP verification can be rolled; patch currently in release-engineering queue.
- Index rebuild for route_aliases requires a maintenance window with low traffic — product to confirm acceptable window.

Open questions / discussion points:
- Should routing policy invalidate route metadata cache synchronously on config-push or rely on shorter TTL? (Carlos pref recommends synchronous invalidation for safety; tradeoff: config-push latency).
- For quotas: do we prefer stronger consistency (fewer overdrafts) at cost of extra RPCs per request, or eventual consistency with periodic reconciliation? Need product input — tagging product team.

Notes to self / rough ideas:
- Follow up with product-hosted-api on quota semantics and acceptable failure modes.
- Add a small load test focused on alias-heavy traffic to verify index fix under realistic concurrency.

Next standup: 2026-03-19 09:30 PT

Attachments / refs: PF-4123, PF-4180, PR #678, brief runbook draft at Confluence page linked above.

(Informal notes — meeting was a mix of quick updates and triage. Leaving this as a working doc until cutover complete.)
